items.excerpt:
There's a lot of stuff in this new release of my LLM CLI tool and Python library, representing around two months of accumulated features and fixes.
I added gpt-6.1-sol and gpt-6.1-terra , plus a new llm openai endpoint add command to make it easier to configure additional models that use OpenAI-compatible endpoints.
I switched the default model (if you have not set your own default) to gpt-6-luna - half the price of the previous default, gpt-5.6-luna .
LLM's support for embeddings now accepts that different binary content may have different content-type - necessary for models like Gemini Embedding 2 , which can embed text, audio, images, and video.
A lot of open source maintainers complain about a flood of AI-assisted PRs. LLM is my project that has been most affected by this and, to be honest, I'm not finding it to be a problem. That's mainly because I have Opus 5.5 or GPT-6 Astra help me with triage to spot the most useful fixes!
This release includes fixes from 12 authors - almost all AI-assisted - and the burden of reviewing them wasn't nearly as great as I expected. I really see them as bug reports with attached examples - sometimes I land them, sometimes I implement my own fix.
So thanks to 0d00ciallo0721 , ac1982 , Allen Flux , Bian Yuhan , Bishop Kammeraad , Chen Yufeiyang , Christopher Krah , Ethan Stoner , Jiachen Xie , Olamide Faniyan , Sharat Chandra Sai Boddu , nosmile99 for helping out with (or spending tokens on) this release!

items.description: Evals without traces, million-cell tabular reviews, and cracks in the billable hour as a business model
items.excerpt:
Evals without traces, million-cell tabular reviews, and cracks in the billable hour as a business model
In this episode, we chat with Jacob Lauritzen, CTO of Legora, following the announcement of their $550M Series E at an $8.8B valuation a couple weeks ago. We talk about what it takes to build AI agents for lawyers and what other people building agents can learn from that work.
Legora started in a Stockholm basement with a simple product: ChatGPT, Swedish law, and a search tool. Jacob had already been through YC with his own startup when he helped Max Junestrand with the application for Leya (now Legora). He later joined as head of engineering and is now CTO.
Today the agent drafts and edits Word documents, reviews thousands of contracts at once, and coordinates work between lawyers, their clients, and other agents. The company passed $100 million in ARR in April, less than 18 months after launch, and now has more than 1,800 customers. It raised $550 million in March at a $5.55 billion valuation, then another $550 million in October at an $8.8 billion valuation. Its latest acquisition, Wexler, was its fifth just this year.
We asked Jacob how you evaluate agents when you can't see your customers' data, which tasks still need better models, how legal engineers and forward deployed engineers split the work, and why the billable hour as a business model is being upended.
When Jacob first read Leya's YC application, he had one piece of feedback: people had tried building legal tech a million times, and it never worked. If lawyers bill by the hour, getting faster means earning less. Why would they buy a tool that does that?
What changed, he says, is the pressure on firms. In the US, routine work like small reviews is already shifting to flat project fees. Some firms do it for free to hold on to the client. The money moves to M&A, litigation, and time spent with clients.
We asked whether that means firms will stop needing paralegals and junior lawyers. Jacob says that's not what Legora is seeing. A good junior is worth more today than two years ago because they get so much more done, just as in engineering.
Most teams improve their agents by reading traces. Legora can't read any. Almost everything users upload is confidential, and much of it belongs to the firm's clients, not the firm.

Legora can’t read a single trace of what its agent does for a lawyer. The data belongs to the law firm’s clients. How do you build and test an agent when you can’t see its work?
Jacob Lauritzen is the CTO of Legora, one of the fastest-growing companies in legal tech history. The team started in a Stockholm basement with ChatGPT, Swedish law, and a search tool. Today, a lawyer can use Legora to draft and edit Word documents, review 10,000 contracts in a single table, or run due diligence. The agent also coordinates work between lawyers, clients, and other agents. When Legora made its own acquisitions, the team used it for diligence.
• Why Legora resisted adding a model picker for years, and why it finally added one
• Jacob’s estimate that models already do about 60% of legal work well, and why the rest takes a smarter model

• Why drafting a long contract is a search problem
• Whether model labs will cut off legal tools the way they cut off coding tools

items.excerpt:
By Gleb Tsipursky , PhD, CEO, Disaster Avoidance Experts
A new industrial robot can meet its cycle-time target and still fail its most important workplace test: what happens when an experienced operator believes the machine is wrong?
That question deserves attention as manufacturers accelerate automation. The International Federation of Robotics reported in September that the global stock of industrial robots exceeded five million units in 2025, with more than 600,000 new installations that year.
Increased capacity is real. So is the need to know how employees can challenge the system before a mistake spreads across a shift.
The latest performance improvements make the issue more urgent. As Robotics & Automation News reported on October 20, ABB’s new IRB 1700 models promise up to 20 percent shorter cycle times , with precision and energy-efficiency gains.
Faster cycles help a business meet orders. They can also reduce the time in which a worker identifies and explains an unexpected result. Speed magnifies the value of a clear escalation process.
In a recent opinion on simulation before deployment , BlueBotics CEO Nicola Tomatis made a useful case for testing traffic, charging, routes and fleet capacity while changes remain inexpensive. There is another variable worth testing before a system goes live: the human response to a disagreement.
Imagine a machine-vision system marks a batch of parts as defective. A veteran operator suspects residue on the camera lens, not a production defect. The automated workflow is ready to divert the batch.
Who can challenge that classification? Can they pause the quality decision without compromising machine safety? Which supervisor receives the evidence? Does the next shift know what happened? This is a hypothetical example, but the questions are ordinary operational ones.
Safety procedures must remain separate and paramount. OSHA’s robotics guidance notes that many accidents occur during non-routine operations such as testing, setup, maintenance and adjustment.
A disagreement protocol cannot replace physical safeguarding, lockout/tagout, emergency stops or task-based risk assessments. Workers should never have to enter a robot’s hazardous operating area to contest an automated recommendation.

items.description: OpenAI 自 GPT-5.6 起在其最强模型的内部和外部流量上部署激活分类器（probes），利用模型内部激活逐 token 实时评分，可在生成中途阻断违规回复和工具调用并交由推理模型复审。实验显示 probes 比更大的文本分类器对测试的越狱攻击更鲁棒，准确率随模型能力提升，且在后训练各检查点间迁移良好，但需为新基础模型重新训练，且只能检测可显式训练的已知违规类型。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/wlmiqh13694tqabyvu6nzvlrs

Training activation classifiers for safety and alignment
OpenAI 自 GPT-5.6 起在其最强模型的内部和外部流量上部署激活分类器（probes），利用模型内部激活逐 token 实时评分，可在生成中途阻断违规回复和工具调用并交由推理模型复审。实验显示 probes 比更大的文本分类器对测试的越狱攻击更鲁棒，准确率随模型能力提升，且在后训练各检查点间迁移良好，但需为新基础模型重新训练，且只能检测可显式训练的已知违规类型。
OpenAI 官方披露激活分类器的架构、训练与部署细节，并给出其相对文本分类器在越狱鲁棒性上的实验对比。
2026年11月2日 · Alex Makelov, Xiaojun Xu, Sundaram Ananthanarayanan, Ethan Mcdonald, Tom Dupre la Tour
我们将激活分类器（又称探针）训练并部署为额外的一层安全防护，用于我们能力最强的模型。探针是高效的实时监控器，利用模型内部的激活值来检测可能违反策略的行为。
探针是对其他安全措施的补充，而非替代。探针通过监督方式训练，因此只能检测我们能够明确训练它去检测的内容。由于探针依赖被监控模型的激活值，新的基础模型需要重新训练探针，而且随着模型权重变化，可能也需要重新训练。
在 OpenAI，我们训练模型以安全、对齐的方式行事。尽管这一方向近来取得了进展 [OpenAI, 2026b] ，但仍存在一些情况：对抗性压力、罕见情形或训练失败可能削弱安全性与对齐。为此，我们采用“纵深防御”策略：在部署模型时附加监控器，用于检测这类情况并阻止模型进一步行动。具体来说，我们使用运行在用户提示词和助手回复上的文本分类器来实现这一目的。从 GPT-5.6 起 [OpenAI, 2026a] ，我们在这套防护体系中又增加了一层：运行在所有助手回复上的 激活分类器 。
激活分类器，简称 探针 ，是轻量级机器学习模型，利用 LLM 自身的内部激活值——即它的“神经模式”——来判断模型活动是否偏离对齐或存在其他不良情况（例如用户活动带有有害意图）。与外部基于文本的分类器相比，探针有多项优势：它们支持 流式 决策，可以在模型某一轮对话进行到一半时拦截违反策略的内容；面对越狱攻击，比规模大得多的文本分类器更稳健；运行效率也显著更高。此外，探针的准确率通常随模型能力同步提升：在能力更强的模型激活值上训练的探针，本身就是更强的分类器。
探针的一个根本局限在于依赖有标注的训练数据；我们只能用它检测已知且可测量的不良活动类型。探针还有一些运行层面的限制，源于它与被监控模型前向传播的紧密耦合。在一个模型激活值上训练的探针，与权重初始化不同的另一个模型的激活值不兼容。尤其是，每出现一个新的预训练基础模型，探针都需要重新训练。即便在同一基础模型系列内，随着模型权重偏离训练探针时所用的检查点，探针性能也可能下降，因此需要定期重新训练 [见迁移部分] 。
我们已在能力最强的模型的内部和外部流量上部署了探针。它是我们 内部失准监控系统 的一个组成部分，与基于模型的审查、自动化调查和人工响应并列。这篇博文介绍我们的方法以及一些重要发现。下图数据来自各项内部实验，未必能代表实际部署的分类器。
探针以残差流激活向量为输入（通常取自模型中间某一层），输出对应二分类任务的 logits（例如预测某段补全是否违反给定策略）。
我们的架构基于 Attention probes [ Kantamneni et al. (2025) ]，采用 MLP + QV-attention 结构，并加入指数移动平均。 1 与滚动均值（[ McKenzie et al. (2026) ]、[ Kramar et al., 2026 ]）相比，指数移动平均把探针的流式状态内存从 O(window_size * num_heads) 降到 O(num_heads) 。实践中我们发现，两种方法的预测能力基本没有差别。我们还额外加入了一个可学习的 pre-MLP 偏置，其初始值取自训练激活均值（负值）的估计；我们发现这能让训练中的优化更稳定。在许多领域，我们训练多输出探针，在共享探针大部分权重的同时提高分类的粒度。这有助于某些训练数据有限的输出类别更好地泛化。
在选择架构的过程中，我们做了鲁棒性实验，检验探针预测对助手消息中违规后缀之前所放置的良性 token 序列是否保持不变。我们观察到，MultiMax 探针架构 [Kramar et al., 2026] 受良性前缀的影响明显大于 Max of Rolling Means Attention 架构 [Kramar et al., 2026] ，而后者与我们的指数衰减注意力架构非常相似（图 1）。

Warehouse automation is advancing quickly. Automated storage and retrieval systems, autonomous mobile robots, robotic picking, sophisticated warehouse management systems, and increasingly intelligent execution software are changing how goods move through distribution facilities. But installing more technology does not automatically create a modern warehouse. In many operations, the physical technology is advancing faster than the operating model surrounding it. A warehouse may introduce robotics into one process, automated storage into another, and new software on top of both, while still relying on procedures, labor structures, and decision-making processes originally built around predominantly manual operations.
That mismatch is becoming increasingly important. As fulfillment requirements become more complex, warehouse modernization needs to move beyond a discussion about which technology to deploy. The bigger question is how the operation itself must change when people, software, and automation increasingly perform work together.
From a Manual Operation to a Technology-Enabled System
Historically, warehouse operations were designed largely around the movement of people. Workers traveled to storage locations, searched for inventory, picked products, moved carts or pallets, sorted orders, and delivered goods to packing and shipping areas. Warehouse management systems helped coordinate this activity, but execution ultimately depended heavily on people moving through the building. Automation changes that fundamental relationship.
In a goods-to-person environment, for example, the employee may remain at a workstation while inventory moves to that person. An AS/RS can replace portions of traditional storage and retrieval activity. Mobile robots can take over transportation between operating areas. Robotic picking can potentially shift additional handling activities away from employees.
As those technologies accumulate, the warehouse becomes less like a collection of independent processes and more like an interconnected operating system. This is important because the performance of one technology increasingly depends on everything around it. items.excerpt:
The Association for Advancing Automation (A3) has announced the publication of ISO 21423:2026, a new international standard for communication and interoperability among industrial mobile robots (IMRs), regardless of vendor or model.
ISO 21423 provides a common set of communication requirements for mobile robots from different suppliers operating in the same industrial facility.
Developed by ISO Technical Committee 299, ISO 21423 Robotics – Industrial mobile robots – Communications and interoperability specifies how IMRs, IMR fleet managers and other equipment exchange information and request actions. Robots can share their location, speed, direction, condition, tasking and availability with each other.
For end users, this means fewer cases of robots interfering with each other’s paths or path planning, which improves robot availability and system efficiency.
A common protocol is also expected to increase competition in the market and support innovation. An important benefit of an ISO standard on this topic is that it can be adopted in countries all around the world.
Carole Franklin, A3’s director of standards development, robotics, says: “Companies want to choose the robots that fit their applications and have those robots work together on the same floor.
“Many leading industrial users of mobile robots have asked for an interoperability standard for years. Now, ISO 21423 gives manufacturers and users a common basis for communication across fleets, no matter where in the world their facility is located.
“This standard can help companies expand automation with equipment from different vendors and make better use of the robots they already have.”
The standard also covers communication with machines tended by robots, enterprise resource planning (ERP) tools, and industrial building systems such as lifts, automated doors and alarms. People using mobile devices can share similar information, so their work can be coordinated alongside the robots.
ISO 21423 represents the first non-safety robot standard that A3 has helped produce, and highlights A3’s continued leadership in the robotics standardization efforts.
ISO 21423:2026 is available for purchase through the A3 online store for $373. A3 members can purchase the document for $320.

items.description: Where Decision Intelligence Goes Next: From Recommendations to Governed Action is the next logical stage of the category. Many platforms can already surface an insight or recommend an action. The post Where Decision Intelligence Goes Next: From Recommendations to Governed Action appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
The next stage of Decision Intelligence is not simply better recommendations; it is governed action. Many platforms can already surface an insight or recommend a response, but the harder step is connecting that recommendation to explicit authority, executable workflow, and feedback so the organization can act faster without losing control.
Instead of generating a one-time answer, decision systems will increasingly monitor a class of decisions continuously, maintain the relevant context, and update the recommendation as state changes. That persistence is essential in supply chains because orders, inventory, capacity, risk, and execution status are always moving. The move from recommendation to governed action is the natural extension of Engineering the Decision Architecture , where context, authority, escalation, and execution are designed as one operating pathway.
ERP, planning, TMS, WMS, visibility, risk, and network platforms remain systems of record and execution; decision intelligence sits above and across them where context is assembled, tradeoffs are evaluated, actions are prioritized, and responses are coordinated. The architecture needs controlled mechanisms for a recommendation to become a transaction, workflow change, communication, or other physical-execution instruction.
Low-risk, frequent, reversible decisions can move first. Higher-value decisions may remain machine-recommended and human-approved. Novel or relationship-sensitive situations should escalate. The market will differentiate on how well providers encode these boundaries rather than on whether they use the word autonomous.
Buyers will require traceability into data used, options considered, approvals, confidence, actions, overrides, and outcomes. That record supports trust, compliance, performance improvement, and the gradual expansion of machine authority where evidence justifies it.
The provider archetypes—planning and optimization-led; visibility, event, and risk-led; decision-orchestration and AI-native; and suite, network, or enterprise-led approaches—will increasingly overlap around the signal-to-action loop. Cloud migration is the process of moving an application, its data, and its infrastructure from on-premises servers to a cloud provider’s environment.
In legacy modernization it usually comes up first, because it promises quick gains in hosting costs and availability.
Its limits often show up a few months later, when changes still take as long to ship as before, now on infrastructure billed by the hour.
Well-planned software modernization services ( https://www.merixstudio.com/services/software-modernization ) treat the move to the cloud as one track of a broader roadmap, next to refactoring, test automation, and UX work.
This article is most useful for CTOs and IT managers deciding whether lift and shift is the right first step for their legacy system.
Lift and shift, also called rehosting, moves an application to cloud infrastructure with minimal changes to its code. Servers, storage, and backups move to the provider, and adding capacity becomes a configuration task instead of a hardware purchase.
Everything above the infrastructure layer stays where it was. A release that needed a week of manual regression testing still needs it, and users see the same interface. For this reason, lift and shift should be judged as an infrastructure decision. Its effect on development speed is indirect.

Speed is the main advantage. A lift and shift migration can take as little as two to three months, while refactoring a mid-complexity system typically takes four to eight.
Migration falls short when the reasons for modernizing sit in the code. Common signals include simple changes that take weeks to ship, thin test coverage that turns every release into a manual exercise, and a monolith that can only scale by renting a bigger machine.
Costs are the less obvious risk. An application designed for fixed on-premises servers usually runs at a constant size, and in the cloud idle capacity is still billed.

items.excerpt:
Each October since 1945, the U.S. Department of Labor has sponsored National Disability Employment Awareness Month to acknowledge the positive impact people with disabilities have on the American workplace. This year’s theme was “Celebrating Value and Talent.”
Despite mounting evidence that hiring people with disabilities makes good business sense, corporate America has a long way to go in that regard. People with disabilities often face a number of hurdles in finding work. They not only must overcome their disabilities but also must fight inaccurate hiring assumptions. One misconception is that employees with disabilities won’t be there for the long haul, yet studies have shown that workers with disabilities actually have lower rates of turnover than the general staff.
As for concerns about performance, the evidence shows that facilities that hire workers with disabilities perform as well as—or better than—similar operations. A 2023 study by Accenture , in partnership with Disability:IN and the American Association of People with Disabilities, found that companies that employ and support people with disabilities outperform their peers without such programs. They reported 1.6 times more revenue, two times more profit, and 2.6 times more net income than those without a disability hiring program.
It doesn’t take much to adapt a facility for this workforce. Research from the Job Accommodation Network shows that more than half (56%) of accommodations cost nothing at all to implement, while others average around $300. That’s a small price to pay to expand the talent pool.
As for what those accommodations might entail in our corner of the world, many warehouses would require only simple changes. For instance, companies could design picking and packing stations to accommodate wheelchairs. They could provide workers who have visual disabilities with voice systems to provide directions. Likewise, they could equip those with hearing impairments with screens or use pick-to-light systems for guidance.
Simple adaptations can also be made for workers with cognitive issues and learning disabilities, like difficulty reading letters and numbers. For instance, one Walgreens facility I visited used snack-food symbols rather than numbers to designate picking aisles.
It’s difficult finding quality workers these days. Don’t overlook a ready-and-willing workforce of people who only ask for an opportunity.

items.title: How AI Applications Earn Their Premium
items.description: Cheaper intelligence raises the bar for what an AI application can charge
items.excerpt:
Lower inference costs can improve margins for application companies, but more capable models and easier development tools can also make parts of an application easier to replace. The commercial question is what customers will continue to pay for as their alternatives improve.
This exposure varies by product. An application is vulnerable when a customer can reproduce its core output with a general-purpose model and little ongoing effort. This is the question for AI application companies right now. Pricing is always important, but right now it’s extra important , yet it sometimes gets overlooked or postponed because fast-growing AI companies are reluctant to tackle it.
All AI application companies need to spend time rigorously developing and pricing out these obvious-but-necessary capabilities: Domain expertise, deep integrations, reliable execution, and hard-to-access context. These are all pricing levers that can make buying substantially more attractive. Founders need to understand which advantages their customers actually value, then strengthen and price them.
The resulting build-versus-buy test looks like this:
Repsol’s legal team put the build-versus-buy question to a direct test. In a blind evaluation, it compared Harvey with Microsoft Copilot and its own internal AI prototype, Lexia. Harvey delivered the highest-quality output, then outperformed the alternatives on accuracy and time savings during an eight-week pilot involving 50 lawyers across 12 jurisdictions. Repsol proceeded with a full rollout. Harvey reports that lawyers now save four to six hours per week, with adoption reaching 96% across the legal department. The benefits also extend to future work: the team used Harvey to identify recurring objections across past agreements and improve its contract templates with fallback language. The case illustrates how an application can earn its premium through better execution than credible alternatives, measurable savings, and the ability to turn accumulated knowledge into reusable guidance. 1
From this and other examples, we gather three rules for sustained success:
Operate the workflow better than the customer can
Make context cheaper to rent than to rebuild
Prove the value, then price to capture it
A customer does not need to rebuild your entire application to weaken your pricing power. Moving one high-volume task in-house or establishing a credible alternative can be enough to challenge the premium.

OpenAI 推出 Grid Protectors 计划，与电力公司、监管机构和政策制定者合作，让未来算力校园在电网紧张时降低用电需求，首站为 Effingham County 校园。
OpenAI 首次系统化说明其校园电力弹性安排，给出 Georgia Power 合同的具体可削减容量与电费影响数据。
今天我们启动 电网守护者计划 （Grid Protectors Program），这是一项全国性行动，旨在让我们建设园区所在社区的居民和企业用上可负担、可靠的电力。我们将与公用事业公司、监管机构和政策制定者合作，为未来的园区制定安排，在电网承压时降低用电需求。
无论是北方寒潮来袭时供暖，还是南方热浪期间开空调，家庭都需要可靠的电力。我们的目标是让园区的灵活性成为一种资源，在社区最需要的时候供公用事业公司调用。
预计到2030年，美国数据中心容量将超过 100吉瓦⁠（在新窗口打开） ，我们因此迎来一个千载难逢的机会：通过建设能在社区最需要时调整用电的园区，来强化电网。
佐治亚州是我们的起点。通过电网守护者计划，我们希望让这种灵活性成为未来园区建设和运营的核心组成部分。这意味着在设计设施时就考虑在需要时降低用电，并与公用事业公司商定可削减多少需求、多快削减以及持续多久。具体安排将因地点而异，相关承诺一旦敲定，我们会另行公布。
根据当地需求和可用设备，我们还将与电网运营商合作，由现场发电或储能供电，并利用电池和功率控制来平抑需求波动。
无论需求高低，输电线、变电站及其他电网基础设施的建设都是固定成本。通过在电网有余量时多用一些电、在电网承压时减少用电，我们可以帮助分担这些基础设施的成本，同时减少为满足峰值需求而进行昂贵升级的必要。这有助于为其他用户压低成本。
美国需要更多电力来支撑经济增长，而AI正成为其中相当大的一部分需求。家庭和小企业不应被要求为计算园区的用电买单。我们始终承诺自行承担能源成本，包括我们使用的电力以及服务园区所需的基础设施。大型计算设施应当支付自身成本，并帮助公用事业公司管理它们所依赖的系统。

这意味着我们可以调低用电需求，让家庭、小企业和其他电费用户继续有电可用。建设电网资产成本高昂，佐治亚电力公司表示，这种灵活性可以减少其为满足未来增长而需要新建的发电装机。虽然园区仍在开发中，但我们希望 Effingham 能成为 Grid Protectors 的试点，这建立在现有协议的基础上，而该协议已经为未来的园区提供了范本。
想象一下度假小镇上的一家餐厅。旺季时它需要足够的餐桌和厨房空间，但全年都得为这些容量付费。老顾客帮它维持使用率，在旅游淡季时帮着分摊账单。我们提议的就是做那个老顾客。

items.description: Dematic’s Adam Brown discusses how simulation, flexible automation, and inventory planning can help warehouses prepare for disruption.
items.excerpt:
Warehouse leaders can’t predict every disruption , but they can prepare their facilities to adjust when plans fall apart. In this Q&A, Adam Brown , Senior Director for Market Intelligence at Dematic , discusses how simulation and flexible automation can help, and when it makes sense to rethink facility locations and inventory storage.
Supply Chain 24/7: You can’t plan for every disruption. So what makes a warehouse ready to handle something nobody saw coming?
Adam Brown: You can’t foresee every disruption, but you can prepare by identifying where your operation can adjust. If one piece of equipment goes down, can workflows adapt? If orders spike, do you know which part of the warehouse will reach its limit first? You may not know what the next disruption will be, but you can better understand how your operation is likely to respond.
That preparation goes beyond equipment. Employees need to know what to do when the normal process is interrupted, and backup plans need to be tested before anyone has to rely on them.
Software is a great solution to help teams spot trouble sooner. For example, Dematic Command Center brings together intelligence from across the system so teams can see where performance is slipping and what needs attention. That gives them time to act before a small issue becomes a bigger operational challenge.
SC247: What’s a warning sign that a warehouse will struggle if demand suddenly jumps or the mix of orders changes?
Brown: A clear warning sign is when a relatively small change in demand creates a disproportionate increase in backlogs. If a modest jump in orders requires sustained overtime just to stay on schedule, the operation may not have room to absorb a larger disruption.
Order mix matters as much as total volume. A warehouse designed primarily to fulfill orders for retail stores may struggle when its order mix shifts toward e-commerce . Even if the overall number of units stays the same, the work required to fulfill those orders has changed.
Look at where work consistently piles up. That’s often where the right automation solution can make the biggest difference. Understanding those pressure points helps you choose the right approach, whether that means introducing more flexible automation or expanding an existing automated system. Planning for how that change affects the next step in the process helps the whole operation keep pace as demand grows.

items.title: Report: One in Four Leaders Regret Their Warehouse Automation Choice
items.description: One in four supply chain leaders regret their warehouse automation choice, while 94% say switching providers would be prohibitively expensive.
items.excerpt:
One in four supply chain leaders wish they had made a different warehouse automation decision, according to a new Exotec report. But changing course could be costly, as 94% say switching providers would be prohibitively expensive.
“Avoid Robot Regret” surveyed 250 supply chain decision-makers in the U.S. and Canada . The warehouse robotics company found that disappointment often starts with decisions made before a system is installed, including how buyers calculate costs and assign responsibility when something goes wrong.
“What we heard from supply chain leaders is that regret is rarely about the technology itself,” said Romain Moulin, CEO and co-founder of Exotec. “It starts when a system built by several vendors stops working as one, and the customer is left figuring out who is responsible for the fix. The operations that get the most from their automation are the ones where a single partner owns the whole system performance, from design through the years it runs.”
Larger companies also reported problems with their automation investments. Among respondents at companies with more than $1 billion in revenue, 21% said their biggest automation investment fell short of expectations, compared with 13% at smaller companies.
Nearly two-thirds of respondents, or 65%, said their total ownership costs were higher than expected. Yet 69% admitted they did not calculate the full lifetime cost before investing.
The report points to expenses that can be missing from an initial proposal, such as software and hardware upgrades or spare parts. Seven in 10 respondents said undisclosed automation costs had increased their annual maintenance expenses.
Overruns were biggest among buyers whose systems fell short of expectations. Within that group, 43% said total costs were 26% to 100% higher than anticipated.
Most respondents (60%) had automation designed by multiple companies. One in seven leaders said they had not seen the benefits of automation because no vendor took full responsibility for system performance.
The report urges buyers to establish who will handle problems before signing a contract. It also recommends asking what maintenance includes and how support will continue if the project manager leaves.
Preparation was another trouble spot. More than a quarter of respondents, or 27%, said their warehouse wasn’t ready when they invested in automation.

items.title: Govern the Living System: Change Control and Lifecycle Management
items.description: The governance intensity around a logistics system is often highest right before go-live and lowest during the years when the system actually creates value or accumulates debt. That is backwards. Go-live is the start of the operating lifecycle, not the end of the engineering work. The post Govern the Living System: Change Control and Lifecycle Management appeared first on Logistics Viewpoints .
items.excerpt:
The governance intensity around a logistics system is often highest right before go-live and lowest during the years when the system actually creates value or accumulates debt. That is backwards. Go-live is the start of the operating lifecycle, not the end of the engineering work.
The system slowly becomes different from the one that was designed. Systems engineering addresses this through lifecycle management and change control. The Autonomous Logistics Network makes lifecycle governance especially important because decision rights, thresholds, models, integrations, and operating assumptions will all change after deployment.
A logistics system is not finished when it enters live operation. It begins a new phase.
Shipment volumes change. Customers ask for new service levels. Carrier and 3PL networks change. Facilities open and close. New products alter handling and transportation characteristics. Technology vendors release new functionality. Regulations change. AI models require monitoring and retraining. Automation equipment ages.
The architecture has to evolve with these conditions. Lifecycle management provides the structure for doing that deliberately.
The organization needs to know who owns the system, who has authority to change it, how changes are evaluated, how risks are assessed, and how the effect of a change is measured. Without those mechanisms, the operating model gradually fragments.
Functional governance is necessary, but many logistics changes cross functional boundaries. A new carrier-allocation rule may affect transportation, warehouse cutoffs, finance, and customer promises. A warehouse wave-policy change may affect dock flow and linehaul departures. A new AI agent may change decision rights across transportation, fulfillment, customer service, and IT.
The governance model should therefore include end-to-end ownership.
Who is accountable for the performance of the process across functions? Who resolves conflicts between local objectives? Who owns shared data? Who approves changes to automated rules? Who decides whether a local exception should become a global standard?
These questions become more important as technology embeds decisions into the system. Governance is no longer only about approving projects. It is about governing operating behavior.

Humanoid robots are an emerging technology that promises to revolutionize society. Designed and modeled on the human form, humanoid robots can navigate a world made for humans, and it is their versatility that sets them apart from specialized robots, such as automated guided vehicles (AGVs).
Similar to AGVs, humanoid robots need an energy source that can reliably supply power to ensure full operation for as long as required.
While current battery technology has been successful in demonstrating humanoid robot potential, IDTechEx ’s new report Batteries for Humanoid Robots 2027-2037: Technologies, Players, and Forecasts focuses on the technologies that will lead humanoid robots into widespread adoption in the market, reaching 10.5 GWh of battery demand by 2037.
IDTechEx highlights the suitability of current and emerging battery chemistries for humanoid robots. The comparisons illustrate trade-offs between battery performance and technological maturity across different chemistries.
The energy density of a battery used to power a humanoid robot needs to be high enough that it can complete power-intensive tasks and continue operating afterwards. Currently, NMC-based lithium-ion batteries are the most common technology employed by humanoid robots.
They balance a suitably high energy density with the prerequisite specifications of humanoids, that is that they require batteries with the potential to be fast-charged, a good cycle life, and a technology mature enough that they are already, or close to being, commercialized.
The energy density of NMC cathodes can also be improved by increasing the nickel-content in the cathode, which can boost performance and reduce dependence on costly and supply-constrained cobalt.
LFP cathodes are a chemistry considered not energy dense enough to be able to support the general demand of humanoid robots. Since NMC batteries are widely adopted for use in a plethora of other applications, NMC-based lithium-ion batteries are in great supply to support the growth of the humanoid robot market today, and beyond.

As robotics companies race to develop increasingly capable AI models for machines operating in the physical world, TorqueAGI is taking a different approach: supplying the intelligence layer to robot and equipment manufacturers rather than building hardware of its own.
Founded by robotics researcher Dr Ashutosh Saxena , TorqueAGI has spent nearly two years developing and testing what it calls a World-Reasoning Model for industrial robots and heavy machinery.
The company says its approach differs from many vision-language-action models by representing objects, machines and workflows through a spatio-temporal architecture in which physics and geometry form part of the model’s reasoning.
The aim is to enable machines to adapt to changes and learn new tasks from relatively small numbers of demonstrations, while making use of operational data that customers already possess.
Saxena has a long background in robotics and artificial intelligence. He completed his PhD at Stanford University under AI researcher Andrew Ng and later became a professor at Cornell University, where he led the RoboBrain project.
His work on robotic grasping received the Robotics: Science and Systems Test of Time Award in 2023.
TorqueAGI is an Nvidia Perception Partner and was selected for John Deere’s 2026 Startup Collaborator Program.
The company has also worked with Dexterity on truck-unloading robotics and says its technology has been integrated with machines from several major industrial robot manufacturers.

Discussions about car insurance typically focus on premium costs and renewal dates. The vehicle category itself, whether you are driving a hatchback through city traffic or a sedan for daily office commutes, rarely gets the attention it deserves in that conversation.
The type of car you own influences nearly every dimension of your insurance profile. If you are about to buy car policy online, understanding that relationship first will help you make the right decision. The vehicle category determines the risk, and that is why the cover should be chosen accordingly.
Hatchbacks occupy a substantial space in the Indian market. They are predominantly city vehicles.
Add-ons such as zero depreciation cover and return-to-invoice protection may be worth evaluating for newer models. For older vehicles, the calculation changes. What makes sense in year one does not necessarily make sense in year four.

Cover terms and applicable add-ons are subject to the underwriting guidelines of the insurer you choose, so it is worth reviewing those in detail rather than making assumptions.
Sedans fall between the two extremes. They are built for comfort and daily utility, maintaining a proper balance between the two. Their drivers tend to be experienced, their usage is typically regular but not extreme, and the vehicle profile is generally stable from year to year.
A sedan owner’s annual review should also include an honest look at the vehicle’s IDV as it depreciates, and whether the add-ons selected at purchase still serve a purpose.

items.excerpt:
Ice rarely comes up when people talk about industrial automation. It sits far from robotic arms, warehouse vision systems and predictive analytics in the popular imagination.
Yet commercial ice production is going through the same quiet transformation as the rest of the manufacturing floor, driven by the same pressures: rising labor costs, tighter consistency requirements, and the need to do more with less water and energy.
The stakes are higher than they look. Hotels, restaurant groups, event caterers, seafood processors and cold chain operators all depend on a steady supply of ice that meets a defined standard.
Modern ice makers have been automated at a basic level for decades, but the latest generation of equipment goes much further. Below are six shifts manufacturers are making, followed by a look at some of the companies active in the category.
Producing clear ice blocks relies on directional freezing, a slow process that pushes air and impurities away from the freezing front so the finished block is dense and transparent. Done by hand, it depends on an operator watching temperatures, timing the cycle and judging when a block is ready.
Modern equipment hands those decisions to controllers that manage the whole sequence, from filling and freezing through to harvest.
The practical result is repeatability: two blocks produced a week apart look and behave the same, which matters to any operation that sells or serves ice at volume and cannot afford a bad batch.
Temperature probes, water level sensors and pressure readings used to be checked occasionally by a technician walking past the machine. Increasingly they feed continuous data into control systems that track the health of the equipment.
Operators can see when a compressor is working harder than normal or when incoming water quality drifts, and respond before a minor issue becomes downtime.
For a business that needs ice at every service, avoiding unplanned stops is worth more than almost any single feature on a specification sheet, which is why monitoring has moved from an optional add-on to a core part of how equipment is designed.
Water quality largely determines ice quality. Dissolved minerals and trapped air are the main causes of cloudy ice, so manufacturers are automating the stages around the freezer itself: filtration, circulation and the management of impurities that concentrate during freezing.

items.title: When the Spreadsheet Stops Scaling: How to Modernize Cyclical Logistics Across Industries
items.description: Every operations team eventually outgrows the spreadsheet that got them started. A look at how to transform your monthly logistics cycle.
items.excerpt:
Somewhere in your organization, there is a spreadsheet holding things together that shouldn’t be. It was built for a smaller operation. Now it takes minutes to refresh, occasionally fails to load, and requires manual updates every cycle. Leadership lacks a clear operational view. When the person who built it leaves, institutional knowledge leaves with them.
This is not an aviation problem or a healthcare problem or a retail problem. It is an operations problem—and it shows up wherever cyclical logistics are managed at scale. The symptoms are consistent: manual vendor follow-ups, purchase orders updated by hand, no geographic visibility into where inventory actually is, and status checks that take far longer than they should.
The solution is also consistent. A recent transformation in airline in-flight entertainment (IFE) media logistics offers a clear blueprint, and the design principles translate to any supply chain managing cyclical vendor coordination.
Most operational tracking systems start with what’s available—usually a spreadsheet connected to a database. At low volume, this works. As the operation grows, the tooling does not scale with it. Refresh times slow. Columns multiply until the dashboard is unreadable. The process becomes dependent on individuals rather than systems.
The failure modes are predictable. Vendor communication happens when someone remembers to initiate it. Purchase orders are updated by hand every cycle. Status checks that should take seconds take minutes. Nobody has a real-time picture of where things stand across the network.
This pattern appears in healthcare, where inventory managers track surgical supplies across multiple facilities without real-time visibility. It appears in retail, where replenishment teams manage cyclical restocking through trackers that cannot keep pace with transaction volume. It appears in manufacturing, where MRO teams discover that critical spare parts are in the wrong facility only after a line has gone down. And it appears in logistics and freight, where shipment status across a distributed network requires manual aggregation rather than a single live view.
In each case, the data exists. It is simply not surfaced in a way that enables fast, confident decisions.

items.title: Claude Platform 推出 message threads 公测，降低长会话智能体延迟
items.description: Anthropic 在 Claude Platform 推出 message threads 公测，智能体每轮只需发送新增消息而无需重发全部对话历史，从而缩短首 token 时间。 🔗 阅读原文 via AIHOT · https://aihot.news/items/sg5u3u91kw42j1grtyp3ny65n
items.excerpt:
Make long-running agents faster with message threads
Anthropic 在 Claude Platform 推出 message threads 公测，智能体每轮只需发送新增消息而无需重发全部对话历史，从而缩短首 token 时间。
原文给出了 500k 至 1M token 请求下 TTFT 中位数下降约 35% 的数据，以及线程生命周期和接入方式，便于评估长会话智能体的延迟收益。
消息线程功能现已在 Claude 平台开启公开测试。借助消息线程，智能体不必在每一轮都重新发送完整的对话历史，从而降低长时间会话的延迟。
一个编程智能体在一次会话中可能发出数百个请求，而每个请求都会重新发送此前所有的消息和工具结果。当对话达到数十万 token 时，重发全部内容会让 Claude 开始响应前的等待时间变长。使用消息线程后，智能体只发送自上一轮以来的新增内容，从而缩短首 token 延迟（TTFT）。
大多数 Claude Code 用户默认开启消息线程后，50 万至 100 万 token 的请求首 token 延迟中位数下降约 35%。
要使用消息线程，请在 Messages API 请求中添加 thread 参数。第一个请求包含完整对话并开启一个线程，此后每个请求只包含新消息和上一条响应的 ID。在两轮之间，我们会把每个线程保存在内存中，加密存储且不写入磁盘。线程在最后一次请求后 5 分钟过期，之后客户端会重新发送完整对话以开启新线程。虽然使用消息线程后每个请求更小，但 Claude 在每一轮仍会读取完整对话，因此 token 用量保持不变。
消息线程现已在原生 Claude 平台开启公开测试，同时也已在 AWS 上的 Claude 平台、Microsoft Foundry 中的 Claude，以及 Google Cloud 上的 Claude 模型（Anthropic 托管）上线。适用标准 Claude token 费率和现有速率限制。请参阅 文档 开始使用。

Dan Driscoll 将加入 OpenAI，担任国家安全现代化高级顾问，与高层领导和外部合作伙伴共事，就先进 AI 如何加强国家安全和网络安全提供建议，尤其侧重于与美国盟友合作，推动其负责任地使用。
在这一新设职位上，Dan 将与 OpenAI 各团队和领导者，以及政府、产业界、学术界和盟友机构的各方合作，推进务实的现代化举措，推动民主 AI 的建设。他还将帮助 OpenAI 内部团队了解全球国家安全机构的运营需求。
Dan 此前担任第 26 任陆军部长，负责陆军的运营、现代化和资源事务。他的经验涵盖军旅生涯、政府高层领导和私营部门。
在这一职位上，Dan 将为我们的公共和私营部门合作伙伴提供建议，帮助他们推进政策和战略选择的现代化，从而释放 AI 的实际用途，提升国家安全，并帮助确保全球建设的 AI 支持民主原则。他将致力于找出运营需求、机构变革与新兴 AI 能力之间的结合点。Dan 的任命体现了我们帮助民主机构负责任地使用先进 AI、以加强共同安全的承诺，也建立在 OpenAI 与盟友和伙伴合作的基础上——通过其 Daybreak 计划增强网络韧性、保护关键服务。
“AI 应该让人们对自己的生活拥有更多掌控权，人们也应该对 AI 如何发展有发言权。美国拥有非同寻常的机会，与其他国家合作推广民主 AI 的应用。我很高兴欢迎 Dan Driscoll 加入 OpenAI，以加强美国的领导力，帮助我们实现这一目标。”
“我职业生涯的大部分时间都在公共服务中度过，先是作为一名士兵，最近则担任陆军部长和 ATF 代理局长。服役人员理应得到我们能提供的最好的工具。国家安全需求的变化速度比过去五十年任何时候都快。这项技术将帮助他们跟上步伐：减少文书工作，理解更多信息，更快地把正确答案送到正确的人手中。我加入 OpenAI，是为了帮助美国及其盟友负责任地把这项技术投入使用，服务于那些守护我们安全的人。”
Dan Driscoll 曾任第 26 任美国陆军部长。任内，他负责近一百万现役、国民警卫队和预备役士兵以及超过 26.5 万名陆军文职人员的运营、现代化和资源分配。他推动陆军转型，重点在于加快新技术的部署、改革采购流程、打造更有能力的部队。Dan 曾是陆军军官和企业领导者，经验涵盖军旅生涯、法律和私营部门。

items.title: Why physical AI is the next lucrative frontier
items.description: To prove its commercial value, physical AI must get past funding enthusiasm and move into production environments. The post Why physical AI is the next lucrative frontier appeared first on The Robot Report .
items.excerpt:
Genesis AI recently unveiled the Eno robot to bring physical AI into commercial environments. Source: Genesis AI
The fastest-growing market categories have humble beginnings. Physical AI, the combination of robotics and advanced artificial intelligence, is just the latest example.
ChatGPT began as a pitch deck at an accelerator before it became a household name in 2023. Before cloud computing became a boardroom imperative, founders were building it, server rack by server rack, cluster by cluster. And, of course, before fintech rewired retail banking, it appeared as a funding surge in deal flow data that most banks weren’t reading.
You see the pattern, and I’ve watched it repeat itself across several years of evaluating startups. The startup ecosystem is the world’s most underutilized business intelligence system.
Incumbents may amass wealth and power, but it’s the founders who choose to build. Which sectors attract a sudden surge of founding activity is a three-to-five-year leading indicator of where enterprise disruption is headed.
While AI agents garner the lion’s share of media attention and VC funding , deal flow suggests the next market for hypergrowth will be of the metallic persuasion. That is physical AI , which includes autonomous machines and smart manufacturing, among other sensor-laden systems.
Robotics and physical AI startups raised a record $27.6 billion across 1,009 deals in 2025, or more than double the prior year, according to PitchBook. Genesis AI , which emerged from stealth with a $105 million seed round , recently demonstrated a wheeled robot that can bring physical AI into commercially relevant environments without needing to replicate the human body.
Physical AI systems can perceive environments, understand spatial context, make operational decisions, and act autonomously in real time across industrial and other settings. Physical AI systems move beyond static automation toward adaptive operations that continuously improve through interaction with the real world.
As with most tech trends, physical AI is driven by a coalescence of several technologies that have matured simultaneously. These include: multimodal sensing , edge computing, simulation environments, robotics foundation models, and world modeling systems. OpenRouter 发布教程，介绍一个 233 行、仅用标准库的 review.py，通过 Responses API 组合 Files API、Shell 沙箱工具和 Apply Patch 工具，把变更文件上传到托管 Linux 沙箱，让模型实际运行检查确认 bug 并返回 V4A 补丁。
教程给出在沙箱中运行代码验证 bug 的完整脚本与四模型实测数据，读者可照搬接入 pre-push 钩子或 GitHub Actions。
AI 代码审查器会在你推送或合并之前，检查 Git 变更中的缺陷和安全问题。只读 diff 的审查器不得不猜测文件其余部分长什么样，以及怀疑的缺陷在运行时是否真的会失败，而且它给出的修复建议是以文本形式返回，需要你手动复制进去。
本指南中的审查器使用 OpenRouter 的 Responses API ，在 Linux 沙箱中运行你改动的文件，通过运行检查来确认每个缺陷，并以补丁形式返回修复，你可以用参数直接应用。在我们用五个缺陷的变更测试的四个模型中，一次审查耗时一到四分钟，费用在 0.015 到 0.045 美元之间。

你需要 Python 3.11 或更新版本、Git，以及一个从 快速入门 获取、已在 shell 中导出的 OpenRouter API 密钥：
Files API、Shell 工具和 Apply Patch 工具运行在全局端点上（ https://openrouter.ai/api/v1 ）；区域端点会返回 403 。你修改过的文件和上下文文件会被上传到你的 OpenRouter 工作区，并发送给模型提供商，因此只能对允许分享的代码运行该脚本，并确保这些文件中不含机密信息。
两个现有测试仍然通过，因为它们没有覆盖 diff 所改动的部分。（我们的沙箱使用 Python 3.11.14 和 SQLite 3.50.4； unittest 开箱即用，而 pytest 未安装。）

脚本退出时返回 1 ，因为有三项发现是 HIGH 。另有四项发现是通过在沙箱中运行代码 confirmed 的，其命令和输出保存在 .git/ai-review.json 下的 evidence 中。被移除的 conn.close() 是 unconfirmed ，因为 CPython 在函数返回时会关闭本地连接。传入 --apply 即可把打过补丁的 app/orders.py 复制到你的工作树中。
把这个脚本保存为 .git/hooks/pre-push ，然后运行 chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-push ：
当我们在 main 上提交 review.py 、在其上提交包含五个 bug 的改动，并运行 git push origin main 时，钩子执行了审查（ 5 findings, 1 patch, $0.0117, 96 s ），以 1 退出，Git 打印出 error: failed to push some refs 。远端仍停留在上一个提交。
把这个工作流保存为 .github/workflows/ai-review.yml 。我们没有在 GitHub Actions 中运行过这个工作流；我们是在本地运行了相同的 git show 和 review.py 命令。
运行 git show "$BASE:review.py" 时会使用基础分支中的脚本副本，这样拉取请求就无法修改检查它的审查器；而 python -I 会让拉取请求中的文件不出现在 Python 的导入路径上。来自 fork 的拉取请求会跳过该任务， timeout-minutes: 15 则覆盖一到四分钟的审查时间。
在 Settings、Secrets and variables、Actions 下添加 OPENROUTER_API_KEY ，并在你的 分支保护规则 中把 review 设为必需的状态检查。如需更全面的 CI 门禁配置，参见 如何在 CI 中基于 LLM 评估对拉取请求做门禁 。
我们用默认设置和 --context tests/test_orders.py 对上面的示例为每个模型各跑了三次审查。“发现的 bug”统计的是已完成的审查中发现的五个植入 bug。“通过运行代码确认”指模型在沙箱中运行了检查并显示出该 bug。“补丁修复了全部五个”指我们把被接受的补丁应用到一份干净的副本上，并且我们自己的测试对全部五个 bug 都通过。
想要每次审查成本最低（$0.0153），就从 anthropic/claude-haiku-5.5 开始；想要更快的审查（60 秒）以及每次运行都能修复全部五个 bug 的补丁（$0.0447），就用 anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5 （ --model anthropic/claude-sonnet-5.5 ）。你可以在 模型目录 中比较更多模型，并用 Ori Eval 在你自己的仓库上测试它们。
每份评审账单都包含模型 token 费用，再加上 容器 沙箱时间，每秒 $0.0001。Files API 不单独收费（每个文件上限 100 MiB，每个工作区上限 10 GiB，工作区文件不会过期）。
沙箱计费从第一条 shell 命令开始，一直到响应结束，所以评审期间模型思考的时间也算在内。因此，即使 token 便宜，模型越慢，沙箱费用就越高：每次 Haiku 评审的沙箱费用为 $0.0074 到 $0.0159，而更快的 Sonnet 运行为 $0.0047 到 $0.0068。

items.excerpt:
How We Took Over ChatGPT Accounts ( via ) Parameter Labs describe an exploit they found against ChatGPT's implementation of the artifacts pattern (OpenAI used to call this "Canvas" but it looks like the latest revision is called HTML previews ), where interactive custom HTML apps are displayed in a sandboxed iframe.
It's important that HTML in these stays tightly sandboxed to avoid untrusted code interacting with OpenAI APIs and accessing private data.
Parameter found quite a complex attack chain. OpenAI use the MathLive JavaScript library as part of their graph support, and that library includes its own virtual keyboard , which can be triggered in the parent page via postMessage() from the sandboxed iframe.
That message receiving code uses innerHTML , so anything that sends a message can add custom HTML to the parent - and there was no mechanism to prevent other sandboxed frames, including HTML preview frames, from calling that method.
This meant untrusted code in an iframe could insert HTML, and while innerHTML doesn't directly execute script elements it could be used to inject a new iframe without sandbox restrictions.
OpenAI’s CSP rules blocked inline scripts entirely, and only allowed script loading from a handful of domains, but one of those was YouTube - and the YouTube oEmbed endpoint could be used to reflect JavaScript back in a way that executed it.
Once the attack had JavaScript execution on ChatGPT, it was trivial to fetch private user data from APIs and exfiltrate it via an image reference.
The end result: you could create a ChatGPT share URL which, when visited by another signed-in user, could exfiltrate their private data or take actions on their behalf.
OpenAI closed the hole and paid out a $5,000 bug bounty, which I think was a bit cheap for a vulnerability this serious.

IT之家 11 月 1 日消息，美国白宫科学与技术顾问会议主席戴维 · 奥利弗 · 萨克斯（David Oliver Sacks）最近出席 All-In 播客，深入分析 Anthropic 的 S-1 注册文件， 称这家人工智能初创公司很可能成为资本主义历史上最伟大的企业 。
Anthropic 在文件中透露，公司 2026 年上半年营收 163 亿美元 （IT之家注：现汇率约合 1,087.14 亿元人民币） ，账面现金 1,120 亿美元 （现汇率约合 7,469.91 亿元人民币） ，预计 2026 年度经常性收入达 1,000 亿美元 （现汇率约合 6,669.57 亿元人民币） 。通过发行 F 类股票，公司七位创始人将持有 50.1% 的投票权。
戴维 · 萨克斯表示：“我认为，这很可能成为有史以来回报最高的风险投资项目，尤其考虑到这家公司仅成立六年。这也可能是史上价值创造速度最快的风险投资支持企业。”
他继续说道：“Anthropic 拥有超 1000 亿美元现金，他们几乎没有烧掉筹集的钱，简直是资本使用效率的典范。“现在有很多看空 Anthropic 的人认为，这家公司未来承诺的资本开支太高，根本不可能兑现。”
“但这次 IPO 反而为这些承诺提供了保障，因为他们现在已经拥有足够的资金，可以为所有算力订单以及预计中的资本开支提供资金支持。他们实际上只需要募集 800 亿、900 亿或者 1000 亿美元，对吧？这与募集 1500 亿、1750 亿甚至 2000 亿美元完全是两回事，而我之前认为他们需要募集这么多资金。”
“因此，他们在 IPO 过程中对资本市场提出的融资需求会更低，这意味着他们将拥有更强的定价能力，也能够更好地控制流通股数量。我认为，所有这些因素都让我们有理由对 Anthropic 的 IPO 持积极态度。”

items.title: Agents Prompt People: Using Agents for Long-Horizon Financial Work
items.description: Arca's head of AI discusses persistent memory, the benefits of a custom harness, and agentic workflows that span days.
items.excerpt:
Arca's head of AI discusses persistent memory, the benefits of a custom harness, and agentic workflows that span days.
At AI Engineer New York this month, we sat down with Aman Singh , the lead AI Engineer at Arca , an “AI-native” company providing wealth management services.
We discovered that while agents do most of the background work in the firm, there are guardrails in place to ensure that human advisors are making the final decisions. The goal is for AI to guide the process; or as Singh nicely put it, “agents prompt people more than people prompt agents.”
Arca recently raised $48.5 Million in a round led by General Catalyst, with participation from Index Ventures and Venrock.
One of the features of using AI in financial services, explained Singh, is that it’s typically long-horizon work — although not long-running. In his AIE presentation, Singh noted that agent tasks at Arca can take up to ten days. “It's very stop-start, there's many actors in between, many decision points, many handoffs,” he said.
For this reason, Arca has developed an internal memory system .
“So we have this persistence for every client ,” Singh said in our podcast discussion. “What has happened so far? What are we tracking for next? What needs to happen immediately in the next couple of days [and] what are we tracking for the long term? Which individual is responsible for which action? All of this is being tracked by our memory systems that our agents contribute to.”
Arca uses models from frontier labs like Anthropic and OpenAI, with Claude its primary model provider. The company has built its own harness , which automatically selects the best model to use for a particular task, based on the company’s internal benchmarks.
Owning the harness, rather than using a managed agent harness, also means that Arca has the flexibility to change model providers if it needs to.
Safety is obviously key for financial services. Singh noted that although agents do much of the work, an agent’s role is limited to analysis and proposing solutions. Trading and any other money movement is handled by a human advisor.
“All of our safety restrictions are fully deterministic,” he said. “And they take the decision making off the agent's hands.”
In other words, there are certain tools and tasks the agent can execute by itself — but not ones that involve risk to the client. Arca also runs verification checks on known AI security issues, such as prompt injections.

据彭博社10月31日报道，Alphabet、Meta、微软、亚马逊和甲骨文五大巨头承诺未来数年在数据中心等领域投入超过3万亿美元（约20.01万亿元人民币）。其中谷歌支出承诺超1万亿美元、接近一年前的八倍，Meta超8,000亿美元且近半用于最长分30年支付的租约；甲骨文是首家因投资AI数据中心而自由现金流转负的大型科技公司，预计到2028年恢复正自由现金流。
原文汇总五巨头财报披露的支出承诺构成和自由现金流变化，读者可以据此看清各家AI基建投入的规模差异与回收压力。
IT之家 10 月 31 日消息，据彭博社今天（31 日）凌晨报道，AI 基础设施建设仍将吸引巨额资金。Alphabet、Meta、微软、亚马逊和甲骨文五大科技巨头承诺，未来数年将在数据中心等领域投入超过 3 万亿美元 （IT之家注：现汇率约合 20.01 万亿元人民币） 。
随着数据中心建设竞赛愈演愈烈，五家公司披露的租赁、建筑、能源及设备采购承诺大幅增长。这些资金有的将在短期内支出，有的则涉及 未来数十年的长期合同 。
谷歌的支出承诺规模最大。根据 Alphabet 提交的监管文件，包括技术设备、能源和租赁在内的合同承诺总额 超过 1 万亿美元 （现汇率约合 6.67 万亿元人民币） ， 接近一年前的八倍 。
Meta 的支出承诺同样大幅攀升，未来支出总额 超过 8,000 亿美元 （现汇率约合 5.34 万亿元人民币） 。其中将近一半用于尚未生效的数据中心租约，最长分 30 年支付。Meta CFO 苏珊 · 李在上周的分析师电话会议上说：“我们预计将继续大举投资，支持核心业务和新兴 AI 项目。”
今年商界的一大争论，是科技企业斥资数千亿美元建设 AI 数据中心， 究竟能否收回投资 。Alphabet 和 Meta 都是全球最赚钱的企业之一，却因投资有望改变行业格局的新业务，出现 自由现金流由正转负 的情况。
不过，五家公司的支出并非全部用于数据中心，披露口径也不完全一致，因此很难直接比较。
例如，Meta 的部分预算用于 Reality Labs 部门的消费级硬件产品，Alphabet 和亚马逊的计划支出则包括内容授权费用。本次统计也没有计入现有租约和债务等其他大额支出。
五家公司未来的租赁付款承诺合计 1.3 万亿美元 （现汇率约合 8.67 万亿元人民币） ，其他采购承诺合计 1.9 万亿美元 （现汇率约合 12.67 万亿元人民币） 。除微软外，数据均取自各家公司最新财报。微软的采购和建设订单数据来自截至 6 月底的年度报告，该公司此后尚未更新这两项数据。
甲骨文是首家 因投资 AI 数据中心而陷入自由现金流为负 的大型科技公司。在本周早些时候举行的投资者说明会上，甲骨文预计到 2028 年恢复正自由现金流，并计划通过供应商融资和客户预付款等方式，减少项目初期需要自行承担的资金支出。

items.excerpt:
Tokio Marine HCC International (TMHCCI), an insurance company based in Houston, Texas, is partnering with Adrian Flux to launch what they say is “the UK’s first domestic humanoid robot household insurance policy”.
The cover is available to UK customers through Adrian Flux’s home insurance offering, underwritten by TMHCCI.
This new product class is intended to support the development of the emerging customer market. Demand has already emerged in the United States, where robotics and AI companies have launched humanoid robots for the home, with early models on open pre-order at $20,000. Domestic robots are expected to be in UK homes from 2027.
Stuart Heath, head of distribution, international at Tokio Marine HCC International, said: “A robot that costs thousands of pounds is not something you want sitting outside your insurance policy. Insurance has traditionally reacted to rather than facilitated new markets and products.
“TMHCCI has a long-established track record of developing innovative cover, and we are delighted to bring this to market with Adrian Flux.”
Gerry Bucke, general manager, Adrian Flux, said: “As robots start to arrive in people’s homes, we wanted to work with TMHCCI to provide clarity on who is responsible if something goes wrong.
“The new cover is the first of its kind in the UK. Like the driverless car policy we launched in 2016, it will be updated as the technology and the risks evolve.”
It appears to be the world’s first policy that protects your home as well as the robot.
The new policy covers damage to, and theft of, the robot, sudden damage it causes to the home or belongings and personal liability if the android injures someone or damages property.
It also provides emergency recovery or safe disablement of the humanoid following a sudden or unforeseen malfunction.

items.excerpt:
Foundry Robotics has announced its oversubscribed $100 million Series A funding round led by Marlinspike Partners.
Participating in the round are early backers Khosla Ventures and Red Glass Ventures, and new investors SE Ventures, Wing VC, and Axiom Ventures, as well as existing investors Hanabi and Zero Shot Fund.
Foundry builds and operates autonomous factories for complex assembly, combining AI-powered robotic cells with experienced manufacturing experts.
With the new funding, Foundry will build out its Emeryville facility, accelerate deployment of AI models into real-world manufacturing, and grow its robotics research, engineering, and factory operations teams.
Foundry has expanded its manufacturing footprint twentyfold to a 130,000-square-foot facility in Emeryville. The company currently serves defense and commercial industries, focusing on high-value, complex electro-mechanical products where production is constrained.
Applications include drones, autonomous vehicle subassemblies, wire harnesses, underwater vehicles, telecom/data center infrastructure, ground robots, rugged computers, robot compute boxes, satellites, and more.
Foundry has also expanded its multidisciplinary team, bringing together robotics researchers, AI and software engineers, and experienced manufacturing experts to develop, deploy, and continuously improve its technology directly on the factory floor.
“We believe the factories that revive America’s manufacturing sector will need to be rethought from the ground up rather than retrofitting one aspect in an existing factory,” said Adarsh Kulkarni, founder and CEO of Foundry Robotics.
“Our approach is to own the entire final assembly stack and integrate intelligence at every layer – own the buildings that manufacture for our customers while orienting them for robotics deployment. Our mission is to revitalize US manufacturing and create more capacity to build and scale critical product assembly.”
Defense and industrial companies can design new hardware faster than ever, but manufacturing remains a critical bottleneck. Traditional assembly lines are built around a single product, take months to deploy, and are costly to reconfigure.
Foundry takes a different approach, leveraging physical AI to build flexible assembly capacity that deploys quickly, adapts to different products, and scales with demand.

It turns out you cannot have your cake AND eat it
As an engineer-focused newsletter we only very rarely let financial stories through (our last example was Jan 2025 ), but when this is about the future of Google and Google Search , with a recently departed AI leadership, you cannot not care.
At its heart is the tension between overview pages and underlying pages they summarize. Any good enough summary obviates the need for you reading the source. Google’s Featured Snippets or Knowledge Panels have long had that tension with the publishers that supply that data. But now, Google’s own AI Overviews are potentially affecting traffic with… Google's Search revenue.
Google doesn’t break out AI Mode in sufficient detail that we can make any sort of rigorous analysis, but most people are quoting Philipp Schindler (Chief Business Officer):
“It’s worth noting that the strong growth in AI Mode queries had an impact because of the lower monetization we were seeing in AI Mode.”
Together with other bad earnings results it set off a range of steep declines throughout tech:
This is against a backdrop of souring tech/AI sentiment in public markets - and with OpenAI raising at $1.25T not $1.4T , not the sort of thing you want in the lead up to one of the biggest tech IPOs of all time.
